prompt.text: Name a reagent used in organic chemistry
prompt.label: Reagents
prompt.subject: chemistry

answers.name: Chlorine trifluoride
answers.blurb: So reactive it sets fire to sand, glass and asbestos, and an infamous entry in Derek Lowe's "Things I Won't Work With". That fame makes it a much more common answer than it sounds.

answers.name: Diisobutylaluminium hydride
answers.blurb: DIBAL, which turns esters into aldehydes when kept cold. It sounds like a specialist's answer, but every organic chemistry student meets it.

answers.name: AD-mix
answers.blurb: Sharpless's asymmetric dihydroxylation, part of his 2001 Nobel Prize, sold as a ready-made powder: AD-mix-α or AD-mix-β, depending on which mirror image you want. Just add your alkene.

answers.name: α-Halo carboxylic acids and esters
spellings: alpha halo carboxylic acids and esters
